title: Medicare Scam Calls Threaten to Cancel Coverage
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare, saying your coverage will be canceled unless you give them personal information or payment. They may sound urgent and try to scare you.
example_message: "This is Medicare. Your coverage will be canceled unless you confirm your Social Security number and payment details right now."
red_flags: Caller asks for your Social Security number or bank info
Threatens to cancel your Medicare coverage
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you have concerns.

title: Fake Tech Support Pop-Ups on Your Computer
how_it_works: A pop-up appears on your computer saying you have a virus. It tells you to call a number for help. If you call, scammers may ask for money or remote access to your computer.
example_message: "Warning! Your computer is infected. Call Microsoft Support now at 1-888-123-4567."
red_flags: Pop-up has urgent warnings and a phone number
Asks for payment or remote access
Claims to be from Microsoft or Apple
what_to_do: Close the pop-up and do not call the number or give access to your computer.

title: Grandparent Emergency Scam
how_it_works: Someone calls pretending to be your grandchild or a lawyer, saying your grandchild is in trouble and needs money right away. They may ask you not to tell anyone.
example_message: "Grandma, I’m in jail and need money for bail. Please don’t tell Mom and Dad. Send $2,000 right away."
red_flags: Caller claims to be a relative in trouble
Requests money by wire transfer or gift cards
what_to_do: Hang up and call your grandchild or another family member to check the story.

title: Social Media Romance Scam
how_it_works: A scammer pretends to be interested in a romantic relationship online. After gaining your trust, they ask for money for an emergency or travel.
example_message: "I really care about you, but I need help paying for a plane ticket to visit you. Can you send me $500?"
red_flags: Person you’ve never met asks for money
Claims to have an emergency or needs help traveling
Wants to move the conversation off the dating site
what_to_do: Never send money to someone you haven’t met in person.

title: Fake Package Delivery Texts
how_it_works: You get a text saying there’s a problem with a package delivery and you need to click a link or give information. The link may steal your personal details or install malware.
example_message: "Your package is waiting for delivery. Please click here to update your address: [fake link]"
red_flags: Link asks for personal or payment info
what_to_do: Do not click the link. Delete the text and contact the delivery company using their official website if you’re expecting a package.
